headline: ECB Survey: Economists See September as End of Current Hiking Cycle, 2.50% Through End-2027

learning_profile.reason: No relevant ACTIONABLE ECB/context-aware segment was found; current facts and pre-prediction market context determine confidence.

predictions.mechanism: A fully expected 25bp ECB hike limits surprise, while the survey's view that September ends the hiking cycle is equity-supportive beyond the meeting; elevated oil, inflation risk and global yields offset that relief and leave no clean directional edge.
predictions.invalidation: A materially more hawkish ECB signal than the survey implies, or a sharp oil/yield rise, would skew DAX lower; clear confirmation of a terminal hike with falling yields and oil would skew it higher.

predictions.mechanism: The expected 2.50% terminal deposit rate provides some valuation relief, but the hike itself is already priced and current energy-driven inflation and rate pressure cap the bullish read-through for euro-area large caps.
predictions.invalidation: Unexpectedly hawkish ECB guidance plus rising oil/yields would turn the balance lower; a clearly terminal hike and easing energy/rate pressure would turn it higher.

predictions.mechanism: The dovish terminal-rate implication is mildly supportive, but the signal is already largely priced and France remains exposed to the same elevated energy-cost and bond-yield backdrop as the broader euro area.
predictions.invalidation: A hawkish ECB surprise or renewed energy spike would favor downside; lower yields and confirmation that September is the final hike would favor upside.
